newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna stocks propped up by Flughafen demand.
newsitem.headline: Vienna stocks propped up by Flughafen demand.

text.p: Austrian shares pulled their way out of earlier negative territory to end moderately firm on Wednesday thanks to selective buying.
Traders said activity was subdued, but that the bulk of it again centred on demand for Vienna airport operator Flughafen Wien after last week's sell-off offered ample opportunity to buy back stock.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips gained 2.02 points, or 0.2 percent, to 1,030.73 after earlier falling to 1,024.46. Of its constituents, 14 rose, six fell and one was unchanged.
"Demand was very selective," said one trader. "It's utterly quiet in some issues."
Traders said the market's low turnover and the expiry of September futures and options contracts on Friday would likely keep the ATX tethered to its tight 1,020 to 1,040-point range.

The day's best performing blue chip was chip maker Austria Mikro Systeme (AMS), jumping 5.13 percent to 723.3, while the leading decliner was fireproof materials maker Radex Heraklith, down two percent at 294.
"AMS have obviously bottomed out," said another trader, adding there was individual buying interest from abroad but that nobody was willing to sell at present levels.
He expected profit-taking to kick in at around 750 schillings.
Flughafen was by far the most actively traded issue on turnover of 61,425 lots, adding on six schillings to 596.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index gained 0.65 points, or 0.16 percent, to 401.91.
The September ATX future climbed five points to 1,032 on turnover of 1,376 contracts.
